title: Kingdom of Syrmia
capsule: The medieval domain of Syrmia (Srem), occupying the land between the Sava and Danube rivers east of Slavonia, was held as a semi-autonomous banate and later kingdom under Stefan Dragutin, a deposed Serbian king who ruled it from 1282 as a vassal of Hungary after ceding the Serbian throne to his brother Milutin. Dragutin expanded his holdings to include parts of northern Bosnia and Mačva and maintained an elaborate dual position as Hungarian banneret and Serbian prince until his death in 1316. The domain then reverted to direct Hungarian royal control, and its brief kingdom-level status lapsed by the early fourteenth century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Stefan Dragutin's control of Syrmia is documented in Serbian and Hungarian medieval sources, but the precise administrative boundaries of his domain relative to neighboring Hungarian counties are incompletely mapped.
